[abstract]
== Abstract

This document describes the Keyple Demo Ticketing ecosystem from a functional and business perspective. It is intended for project managers, functional architects, and business teams who want to understand the covered use cases without going into technical implementation details. Annexes A and B are a technical reference for the developers: the data model of the card, and the procedures executed on the card.

== Overview

=== Purpose

The Keyple Demo Ticketing is a complete ecosystem illustrating the lifecycle of a contactless transit ticket, from card issuance through access validation to inspection.

It is made available by the *Calypso Networks Association (CNA)* as a starting point for integrators who want to build their own ticketing system based on the Eclipse Keyple middleware.

=== The components

The ecosystem consists of four distinct applications, each covering a specific role in the ticketing system:

[cols="^1,3", options="header"]
|===
| Application | Functional role

| *Sales — server*
| Hosts the security module (SAM) and performs cryptographic operations. Exposes the remote services of reading, loading, and personalization. Its web dashboard (`http://localhost:8080`) displays the status of the server and of the SAM, and the transactions of the clients in real time (see the link:../../src/sales/server/README.md#web-dashboard[server README]).

| *Sales — clients*
| Android, multiplatform (Android, iOS, desktop), or .NET application used by a sales agent or a passenger to load a new transit ticket. The Android and multiplatform clients also personalize blank cards.

| *Validation*
| Terminal installed at access points (gates, validators). Reads the passenger's card, selects the most suitable ticket, and records the entry event.

| *Inspection*
| Terminal used by ticket inspectors. Reads the card, displays ticket details, and checks the validity of the last validation.
|===

=== Ecosystem flow

plantuml::diagrams/overview.puml[target=overview,format=svg,alt="Keyple Demo Ticketing ecosystem flow",align="center"]

NOTE: The validation terminal and the inspection terminal do not communicate over the network. Information is exchanged between these two applications *exclusively through the passenger's card*.

[[scope]]
=== Scope of the demo

The demo covers the personalization of the cards, and the loading, validation, and inspection of season passes and multi-trip tickets. The following elements of the Calypso data model are not covered:

* *Stored value tickets*: they cannot be loaded, and a stored value ticket present on a card (priority 3) is ignored at validation
* *Traceability mode*: the tickets are loaded without the cryptographic authenticator signed by the SAM, and no authenticator is verified at inspection
* *Black lists* of the cards and of the SAMs

The corresponding steps of the procedures are marked _Not implemented by the demo_ in <<card-procedures>>.

[[cards]]
== Contactless cards and media

=== Calypso card

The Calypso card is the primary medium of the ecosystem. It is a smart card compliant with the Calypso standard, enabling:

* Storage of *up to 4 transit tickets simultaneously*, depending on the card product (1 on the Calypso Basic cards, 2 on the Calypso Light cards)
* *Secure transactions* guaranteeing data integrity (via a SAM security module or asymmetric PKI cryptography)

The Calypso card stores in memory:

* Information about the *cardholder and card validity* (issuance date, expiry date)
* Loaded *contracts* (transit tickets)
* The *last recorded validation event*
* *Counters* associated with unit-based tickets

=== Storage cards

Storage cards are simpler memory media without a Calypso security system. They allow lightweight scenarios to be demonstrated:

[cols="^2,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| Type | Characteristics | Authentication

| MIFARE Ultralight
| Lightweight memory card, read/write in 4-byte blocks
| None

| ST25 SRT512
| ST memory card, read/write in 4-byte blocks
| None

| MIFARE Classic 1K
| Sectored memory card, 16-byte blocks
| Secret key KEY_A (sector 1)
|===

NOTE: Storage cards support only *1 transit ticket*. They do not benefit from the same security guarantees as Calypso cards.

IMPORTANT: Storage cards are handled with the storage card extension and reader plugin of CNA, available on request. Without them (default build), the applications do not support storage cards.

With these libraries, the storage cards supported depend on the application and on the terminal:

[[storage-card-support]]
[cols="5,^2,^2,^2", options="header"]
|===
| Application and terminal | MIFARE Ultralight | ST25 SRT512 | MIFARE Classic 1K

| Sales (Android client), validation, and inspection: Bluebird EF501
| icon:check[role=green]
| icon:check[role=green]
| icon:check[role=green]

| Validation and inspection: Famoco FX205
| icon:check[role=green]
| icon:times[role=red]
| icon:check[role=green]

| Sales (Android client) and inspection: other Android devices with NFC
| icon:check[role=green]
| icon:times[role=red]
| icon:check[role=green]

| Validation: Arrive Axio 4
| icon:times[role=red]
| icon:times[role=red]
| icon:times[role=red]
|===

The storage cards are read by the reader plugins configured with the storage card interpreter of CNA: the plugin of the Bluebird terminals, and the Android NFC plugin, used by the Famoco terminals and the other Android devices (this plugin does not support the ST25 SRT512 cards). The plugin of the Arrive terminals does not support them. The multiplatform and .NET sales clients handle the Calypso cards only.

WARNING: This demo is only intended to demonstrate that memory cards can be handled.

== Transit tickets

Two ticket types can be loaded onto a card:

=== Season pass

* Ticket valid for a *30-day period* from the date of sale
* Provides *unlimited access* during its validity period
* *Renewable*: before expiry, the end date is extended by 30 days; after expiry, a new 30-day period starts on the date of sale
* No counter decrement at validation

=== Multi-trip ticket

* *Unit-based* ticket: each validation consumes *1 unit*
* Valid until the *card expiry date* (EnvEndDate)
* Trips can be added by a new loading (up to 16,777,215)
* Remaining trips are visible during inspection

[[ticket-priority]]
=== Ticket priority (Calypso card only)

When several tickets are present on a Calypso card, the validation terminal automatically selects *the highest-priority valid ticket* according to the following ranking:

[cols="^1,3,4", options="header"]
|===
| Priority | Ticket type | Behavior

| 1 (highest)
| Season pass
| Selected first if valid

| 2
| Multi-trip ticket
| Selected if no valid season pass is present and trips are left

| 31
| Expired
| Ignored during validation

| 0
| Empty slot
| Ignored
|===

NOTE: The priority 3 of the data model (Stored value) is not covered by the demo (see <<scope>>).

== Use cases

[[personalization-use-case]]
=== Card issuance and personalization

==== Functional description

Before being used, a blank card must be *personalized*: this operation initializes the card data and sets its validity period.

Issuance is performed from the Android or multiplatform sales client, connected to the server (the .NET client does not personalize cards).

The steps executed on the card are detailed in <<personalization-procedure>>.

==== What personalization does

* Assigns a *unique application number*
* Records the *issuance date*
* Calculates and records the *expiry date*: first day of the current month + 6 years
* Resets all ticket slots, events, and counters to zero

==== Diagram

plantuml::diagrams/personalization.puml[target=personalization,format=svg,alt="Card personalization workflow",align="center"]

'''

[[loading-use-case]]
=== Loading a ticket

==== Functional description

Loading consists of writing a new transit ticket onto the card, or adding trips to or renewing an existing one.
This operation requires the *SAM security module* to be present on the server side.

The steps executed on the card are detailed in <<loading-procedure>>.

==== Process

. The sales agent or the passenger presents the card to the reader of the client (NFC reader of the mobile device, or PC/SC reader of the desktop).
. The server checks that the card is valid (personalized, not expired, last event of a known version), then reads its tickets, which are displayed.
. The user selects the ticket to load.
. The card is presented again: the server checks that a slot is available (with the multiplatform client, that the card is the one read before), then writes the new ticket, the counter being updated if necessary.

==== Business rules

[cols="3,4", options="header"]
|===
| Situation | Behavior

| Card not personalized, expired card, or last event of an unexpected version
| Loading rejected

| Calypso card without free or expired slot
| Loading rejected — no slot available

| Single-ticket card (storage card, Calypso Basic) holding a ticket of another type that is still usable (season pass not expired, multi-trip ticket with trips left)
| Loading rejected

| Ticket of the same type already on the card
| The existing ticket is updated in its slot

| Renewing a season pass
| Not expired: the end date is extended by 30 days from the current end date; expired: new 30-day period from the date of sale

| Loading trips onto an existing multi-trip ticket
| The trips are added to the counter (up to 16,777,215)

| New ticket on an empty slot
| Written to the first available slot

| New ticket on an expired slot
| Replaces the expired ticket at the lowest index
|===

==== Diagram

plantuml::diagrams/ticket-loading.puml[target=ticket-loading,format=svg,alt="Ticket loading workflow",align="center"]

'''

[[validation-use-case]]
=== Access validation

==== Functional description

Validation is the operation performed by the terminal installed at the access point (gate, validator) when a passenger presents their card.

The terminal automatically selects the best available ticket, updates the card data, and records the entry event.

The steps executed on the card are detailed in <<validation-procedure>>.

==== Prerequisites

* The SAM must be present and operational in the terminal.
* Without a SAM, the terminal cannot validate (no fallback mode).

==== Process

. The passenger presents their card to the NFC reader.
. The terminal checks the general validity of the card.
. The terminal analyzes the last recorded event (anti-passback).
. The terminal searches for the best valid ticket among those present.
. If a valid ticket is found: the counter is decremented if applicable, and a new event is recorded on the card.
. The result is displayed to the passenger (access granted or denied).

[[anti-passback-rule]]
==== Anti-passback rule

If the card has already been validated within the previous minute, validation is *rejected* to prevent multiple entries. A message prompts the passenger to wait. The times being recorded to the minute, the effective delay is between 1 and 2 minutes.

NOTE: Special case (Calypso cards only): if the previous validation session was not ratified (card removed before the end of the session), the card presented again within the delay is accepted without a new deduction, the previous session being then ratified.

[[rejected-card]]
==== Rejected card

When no ticket of a Calypso card can be used, the expired or exhausted tickets are marked as such on the card (priority 31), so that the next validations no longer analyze them.

==== Diagrams

===== Calypso card validation

plantuml::diagrams/validation-calypso-card.puml[target=validation-calypso-card,format=svg,alt="Calypso card validation workflow",align="center"]

===== Storage card validation

plantuml::diagrams/validation-storage-card.puml[target=validation-storage-card,format=svg,alt="Storage card validation workflow",align="center"]

'''

[[inspection-use-case]]
=== Ticket inspection

==== Functional description

Inspection is carried out by a ticket inspector equipped with a mobile terminal. It allows the inspector to *check that the passenger holds a validated ticket*, without modifying the card.

The steps executed on the card are detailed in <<inspection-procedure>>.

==== Authentication modes

Unlike validation, inspection can operate *without a SAM* thanks to two fallback modes:

[cols="^1,3,4", options="header"]
|===
| Mode | Activation condition | Level of guarantee

| SAM
| SAM present and available
| Maximum — secure session, cryptographic verification

| PKI
| No SAM, but the card supports PKI mode
| Maximum — asymmetric authentication without external hardware (test certificates in the demo)

| No authentication
| Neither SAM nor PKI available
| None — data read without cryptographic verification
|===

[[inspection-checks]]
==== What inspection checks

* The *general validity* of the card (version, dates)
* The *detail of each ticket*: type, validity dates, remaining trips
* The *validity of the last validation event*:
** Did the event take place at the location configured on the inspection terminal?
** Did it take place the same day, within the configured validation period?
* Which ticket was used during the last validation

[[inspection-display]]
==== Information displayed to the inspector

The inspector sees:

* The authentication mode used during inspection ("`Card authenticated by the SAM`", "`Card authenticated by PKI`", or "`Card not authenticated`")
* The *last validation*: date, time, location, and ticket used
* For each ticket present on the card: its type, its validity period (season pass) or its number of remaining trips (multi-trip ticket), and its status (valid, expired, or validated by the last validation)
* "`No ticket`" when the card has never been loaded

When the card is rejected, the terminal displays "`Not valid on this network`" with the reason (see <<inspection-rejection-conditions>>).

==== Diagram

plantuml::diagrams/inspection.puml[target=inspection,format=svg,alt="Inspection workflow",align="center"]

== Compatible terminals and hardware

This section summarizes the hardware supported by each application. The reader plugins, the installation, and the prerequisites of each component are detailed in the link:../../README.md[README of the repository] and in the README of each application (link:../../src/validation/README.md[validation], link:../../src/inspection/README.md[inspection], link:../../src/sales/README.md[sales]).

=== Tested Android terminals

[cols="^2,4,^1,^1,^1", options="header"]

| Terminal | Description | Sales | Validation | Inspection

| icon:times[role=red]
| icon:check[role=green]

| icon:check[role=green]
| icon:check[role=green]

=== Server and desktop hardware

* *Sales server*: PC/SC reader holding a Calypso SAM, required for personalization and ticket loading
* *Desktop sales clients* (multiplatform and .NET): contactless PC/SC reader

[[sales-clients]]
=== Available sales clients

Three types of clients can connect to the sales server:

[cols="^2,3,3,3", options="header"]
|===
| Client | Platforms | Products | Notes

| *Native Android application*
| Android 8.0+
| Multi-trip ticket (1 to 4 trips), Season pass; card personalization
| Full Keyple framework integration

| *Multiplatform application*
| Android, iOS 15.3+, desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux)
| Multi-trip ticket (1 to 4 trips), Season pass; card personalization
| Shared UI across all platforms

| *.NET desktop client*
| Windows
| Multi-trip ticket only (1 to 20 trips, entered by the user)
| Demonstrates the Keyple Server JSON API (HTTP) without the Keyple framework
|===

NOTE: The prices displayed by the clients are fictitious.

== Results and functional messages

[[validation-results]]
=== Validation results

Each validation produces one of the following results:

[cols="^2,5", options="header"]
|===
| Result | Functional meaning

| *Accepted*
| Access granted, 1 trip deducted for a multi-trip ticket. The terminal displays "`Validation completed!`" with the remaining trips (multi-trip ticket) or the end date (season pass).

| *Rejected*
| Card rejected by a business rule (see below).

| *Not recognized*
| Card not recognized: no supported application ("`Selection error: card not recognized`"), DF name not matching the AID of the application ("`Selection error: unexpected DF name`"), or file structure not supported ("`Invalid card — File structure not supported`"), see <<supported-card-applications>>.

| *Card removed*
| Communication interrupted during the transaction (card removed too early): "`An error occurred. Please try again.`"

| *Failed*
| Unexpected technical error, or failed authentication of a MIFARE Classic card.
|===

[[validation-rejection-conditions]]
=== Validation rejection conditions

[cols="4,4", options="header"]
|===
| Situation | Message displayed

| Card not personalized (environment of an unexpected version)
| Card rejected — Environment error: wrong version number

| Expired card
| Card rejected — Environment error: end date expired

| Last event or ticket of an unexpected version
| Card rejected — Event error / Ticket error: wrong version number

| Card validated less than 1 minute ago
| Card rejected — Card already tapped. Please wait before retrying.

| Card never loaded, or no usable ticket
| No valid ticket detected — Please load a ticket.

| Last analyzed ticket expired
| Expired ticket — Please load a ticket.

| Multi-trip ticket exhausted (0 trips remaining)
| No trip left — Please load a ticket.

| Ticket of a storage card forbidden or expired
| Ticket forbidden or expired — Please load a ticket.
|===

[[inspection-rejection-conditions]]
=== Inspection rejection conditions

[cols="4,4", options="header"]
|===
| Situation | Message displayed (below "`Not valid on this network`")

| No supported application in the card
| Selection error: card not recognized

| DF name not matching the AID of the application
| Selection error: unexpected DF name

| File structure of the Calypso application not supported
| Invalid card — File structure not supported

| Card not personalized (environment of an unexpected version)
| Environment error: wrong version number

| Expired card
| Environment error: end date expired

| Last event of an unexpected version
| Event error: wrong version number

| Ticket of an unexpected version
| Ticket error: wrong version number

| Reading error (for example, card removed too early)
| An error occurred while reading the card.
|===

== Glossary

[cols="2,5", options="header"]
|===
| Term | Definition

| *AID*
| Application Identifier. Unique identifier of the Calypso card application, used when the terminal selects the card.

| *Anti-passback*
| Mechanism preventing a passenger from presenting their card twice within 1 minute, in order to prevent the card from being passed back to another passenger for a second entry.

| *Calypso*
| Open standard for contactless smart cards in ticketing systems, maintained by the Calypso Networks Association.

| *Contract*
| Transit ticket stored on the card. A Calypso card can hold up to 4 contracts simultaneously, depending on the card product.

| *Contract priority*
| Numerical value determining the selection order of tickets during validation (1 = Season pass, 2 = Multi-trip ticket, 31 = expired, 0 = empty slot).

| *Counter*
| Memory area on the card storing the remaining trips of a multi-trip ticket.

| *EnvEndDate*
| Expiry date of the card application (not of an individual ticket). Set at personalization to the first day of the current month + 6 years.

| *Environment*
| Record of the card application holding its version, issuance date, and expiry date (EnvEndDate), written at personalization.

| *Event*
| Record of the last validation operation performed on the card (date, time, location, ticket used).

| *Keyple*
| Open source Eclipse middleware facilitating the development of contactless ticketing applications. See https://keyple.org[keyple.org].

| *PKI*
| Public Key Infrastructure. Asymmetric authentication mode (RSA 2048-bit) that does not require a physical SAM. The demo uses test certificates: a real deployment requires the certificates of its own PKI.

| *Ratification*
| Calypso confirmation that a secure session has been completed. A session interrupted before its ratification (card removed too early) is ratified at the next presentation of the card.

| *SAM*
| Secure Access Module. Cryptographic hardware module used to secure Calypso transactions. Required for personalization, loading, and validation.

| *Secure session*
| Calypso mechanism guaranteeing the integrity and authenticity of data exchanged between the terminal and the card, using a SAM or PKI.

| *Slot*
| Memory location available on the card to hold a contract. A Calypso card has up to 4 slots, depending on the card product.

| *Storage card*
| Simple memory card (MIFARE Ultralight, ST25, MIFARE Classic) that does not support the Calypso protocol. Only 1 ticket possible, no Calypso secure session.
|===

[appendix]
[[card-data-model]]
== Card data model (technical reference)

[[card-data-model-introduction]]
=== Introduction

This annex describes the data model of the Keyple demos: the card applications supported, the structures of the records written on the card, the types of their fields, and the layout of the files and blocks of the cards. It is intended for the developers and the integrators, as the procedures of <<card-procedures>> that use it.

The data model is implemented by the link:../../src/common/README.md[common library] of the demo (classes of the structures and codecs encoding the records): a change of the data model is made both in this annex and in this library.

[[supported-card-applications]]
=== Supported card applications

The demos work with the cards of the https://calypsonet.org/technical-support-documentation/[CNA Test Kit], whose Calypso applications have the following identifiers:

[cols="3,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| AID | Description | Compatibility

| `A000000291FF9101`
| Keyple Generic test card
| All the demo applications

| `315449432E49434131`
| CD Light/GTML Compatibility
| Legacy system support

| `315449432E49434133`
| Calypso Light
| Standard Calypso

| `A0000004040125090101`
| Navigo IDF
| Paris transport system
|===

The DF name of the selected application must start with the AID, followed by zeros only (requirement TL-SEL-AIDMATCH.1 of the Calypso specifications).

The file structure of the application (application subtype) must be one of the following: 01h (Revision 2 minimum), 02h (Revision 2 minimum with MF files), 03h (Revision 2 extended), 04h (Revision 2 extended with MF files), 05h (CD Light/GTML Compatibility), 06h (CD97 Structure 2 Compatibility), 07h (CD97 Structure 3 Compatibility), 08h (Extended Ticketing with Loyalty), 09h (Extended Ticketing with Loyalty and Miscellaneous), 32h (Calypso Light Classic), or 33h (Calypso Basic).

The storage cards (MIFARE Ultralight, ST25 SRT512, MIFARE Classic 1K) are detected by their product type.

[[data-structures]]
=== Data structures

The records have 29 bytes (232 bits) on the Calypso cards, and 16 bytes (128 bits) on the storage cards: the fields are the same, except the padding and the fields related to the SAM. A dash in the "`Storage cards`" column indicates a field not stored on these cards.

==== Environment and holder

Card metadata and holder information, written at the personalization.

[cols="4,^1,^1,6,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Bits (Calypso) | Bits (storage cards) | Description | Type | Status

| EnvVersionNumber | 8 | 8 | Data structure version number | VersionNumber | Mandatory
| EnvApplicationNumber | 32 | 32 | Card application number (unique system identifier) | Int | Mandatory
| EnvIssuingDate | 16 | 16 | Card application issuing date | DateCompact | Mandatory
| EnvEndDate | 16 | 16 | Card application expiration date | DateCompact | Mandatory
| HolderCompany | 8 | 8 | Holder company | Int | Optional
| HolderIdNumber | 32 | 32 | Holder identifier within HolderCompany | Int | Optional
| EnvPadding | 120 | 16 | Padding (bits to 0) | Binary | Optional
|===

==== Event

Last event of the card: validation, or update of the contract priorities.

[cols="4,^1,^1,6,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Bits (Calypso) | Bits (storage cards) | Description | Type | Status

| EventVersionNumber | 8 | 8 | Data structure version number | VersionNumber | Mandatory
| EventDateStamp | 16 | 16 | Date of the event | DateCompact | Mandatory
| EventTimeStamp | 16 | 16 | Time of the event | TimeCompact | Mandatory
| EventLocation | 32 | 32 | Location identifier | Int | Mandatory
| EventContractUsed | 8 | 8 | Index of the contract used for the validation | Int | Mandatory
| ContractPriority1 | 8 | 8 | Priority of the contract #1 | PriorityCode | Mandatory
| ContractPriority2 | 8 | 8 | Priority of the contract #2 | PriorityCode | Mandatory
| ContractPriority3 | 8 | 8 | Priority of the contract #3 | PriorityCode | Mandatory
| ContractPriority4 | 8 | 8 | Priority of the contract #4 | PriorityCode | Mandatory
| EventPadding | 120 | 16 | Padding (bits to 0) | Binary | Optional
|===

==== Contract

Contract (ticket) and its properties.

[cols="4,^1,^1,6,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Bits (Calypso) | Bits (storage cards) | Description | Type | Status

| ContractVersionNumber | 8 | 8 | Data structure version number | VersionNumber | Mandatory
| ContractTariff | 8 | 8 | Contract type | PriorityCode | Mandatory
| ContractSaleDate | 16 | 16 | Sale date of the contract | DateCompact | Mandatory
| ContractValidityEndDate | 16 | 16 | Last day of validity of the contract | DateCompact | Mandatory
| ContractSaleSam | 32 | - | SAM that loaded the contract | Int | Optional
| ContractSaleCounter | 24 | - | SAM authentication key counter value | Int | Optional
| ContractAuthKvc | 8 | 8 | SAM authentication key KVC | Int | Optional
| ContractAuthenticator | 24 | 24 | Security authenticator | Authenticator (Int) | Optional
| ContractPadding | 96 | 24 | Padding (bits to 0) | Binary | Optional
| CounterValue | - | 24 | Number of trips left (storage cards: counter stored in the contract record) | Int | Mandatory
|===

The fields ContractSaleSam, ContractSaleCounter, ContractAuthKvc, and ContractAuthenticator are those of the traceability mode, not implemented by the demo (see <<scope>>): the contracts are loaded with these fields at 0.

==== Counter

Number of trips left of a multi-trip ticket. On the Calypso cards, the counters are stored in a separate file, one counter per contract record; on the storage cards, the counter is stored in the contract record.

[cols="4,^1,6,3,2", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Bits | Description | Type | Status

| CounterValue | 24 | Number of trips left (0 to 16,777,215) | Int | Mandatory
|===

[[data-types]]
=== Data types

[cols="2,^1,8", options="header"]
|===
| Name | Bits | Description

| DateCompact
| 16
| Number of days since January 1, 2010 (date 0). The maximum value is 16,383, the last complete year being 2053. All the dates are in legal local time.

| TimeCompact
| 16
| Time in minutes: hour × 60 + minute (0 to 1,439).

| VersionNumber
| 8
| Version of the data structure: 0 forbidden (undefined: blank record, never written), 1 current version, 2 to 254 reserved for future use (read as unknown by the demo), 255 forbidden (reserved).
|===

[[priority-codes]]
==== Priority codes

The PriorityCode type gives the type of a contract (ContractTariff field) and the priorities of the contracts in the event (ContractPriority fields). Their use by the validation is described in <<ticket-priority>>.

[cols="^1,2,6", options="header"]
|===
| Code | Name | Description

| 0 | FORBIDDEN | Empty record (present in clean records only)
| 1 | SEASON_PASS | Season pass: unlimited travel during its validity period
| 2 | MULTI_TRIP | Multi-trip ticket: one trip used at each validation
| 3 | - | Stored value: defined by the data model, not supported by the demo (read as unknown, never validated)
| 4 to 30 | RFU | Reserved for future use
| 31 | EXPIRED | Contract expired or exhausted
|===

The codes 3 to 30 are read as unknown (`UNKNOWN`) by the demo: a contract of an unknown type is never validated.

[[card-layouts]]
=== Card layouts

Files of the Calypso cards and blocks of the storage cards used by the demo.

==== Calypso cards

[cols="3,^1,4", options="header"]
|===
| File | SFI | Content

| Environment and holder
| 07h
| 1 record of 29 bytes

| Event log
| 08h
| Last event in the record 1 (29 bytes)

| Contracts
| 09h
| 1 record of 29 bytes per contract: 4 records, 2 on the Calypso Light cards, 1 on the Calypso Basic cards

| Counters
| 19h
| 1 counter of 3 bytes per contract record (the counter of the contract #1 first, and so on)
|===

The secure sessions use the access level of the operation, with the default key (KIF) of the SAM: Personalization (21h) for the personalization, Load (27h) for the loading, Debit (30h) for the validation and the inspection.

==== Storage cards

The storage cards hold a single contract, the counter of a multi-trip ticket being stored in the contract record. Their records have 16 bytes, and they have no secure session (no SAM).

[cols="2,2,2,2", options="header"]
|===
| Card | Environment and holder | Contract and counter | Event

| MIFARE Ultralight, ST25 SRT512 (4-byte blocks)
| Blocks 4 to 7
| Blocks 8 to 11
| Blocks 12 to 15

| MIFARE Classic 1K (16-byte blocks, sector 1)
| Block 4
| Block 5
| Block 6
|===

The MIFARE Classic 1K cards are authenticated with the key A of the sector 1 before each reading and each writing. The block 7 of the sector (sector trailer, holding the keys) is never written.

[appendix]
[[card-procedures]]
== Card procedures (technical reference)

[[card-procedures-introduction]]
=== Introduction

This annex details, step by step, the procedures executed on the card by the applications of the demo. It is intended for the developers and the integrators: the use cases of this document describe the same operations from a functional perspective.

The procedures are those of the data model of the Keyple demos, described in <<card-data-model>>. The step numbers are referenced by the comments of the source code (for example, `// Step 11.3.1` in the validation procedure): a change of a procedure is made both in this annex and in the code.

[[card-procedures-conventions]]
=== Conventions

* *Step numbers*: the steps keep the numbers of the data model. The steps added by the demo have a sub-number (for example, 6.1), so that the numbers of the other steps do not change.
* `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`: the card is rejected, the secure session is canceled (no data written), and the procedure ends. On the storage cards, which have no secure session, the procedure ends without writing.
* `<Exit process>`: the procedure ends, the result being returned to the upper layer (the application).
* `END`, `CNT_UPD`, `CNT_READ`: labels of the steps reached by a "`go to`".
* _Not implemented by the demo_: step of the data model that the demo does not implement (see <<scope>>). The step keeps its number, so that an integrator sees where to implement it.

[[detection-selection-procedure]]
=== Detection and selection

Generic procedure, executed by all the applications before the procedures of the following sections.

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

| 1
| Perform the application selection using the AIDs of the demo cards (see <<supported-card-applications>>). The DF name of the selected application must start with the AID, followed by zeros only, and its file structure must be supported by the demo; otherwise, the card is not selected. The storage cards are detected by their product type.

| 2
| If the status of the DF is invalid, report that information to the upper layer. `<Exit process>` +
The validation and inspection terminals do not select the invalidated applications (card not recognized).

| 3
| If the serial number of the selected application is on the black list, go to the step 5. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 4
| Return the information on the selected application. `<Exit process>`

| 5
| Open a validation session without reading any information. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 6
| Send an Invalidate command. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 7
| Close the session. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 8
| Report to the upper layer that a card on the black list has been detected and invalidated. `<Exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._
|===

[[personalization-procedure]]
=== Card personalization

Executed by the sales server, with its SAM (see <<personalization-use-case>>).

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

| 1
| Open a secure session at the Personalization access level, without reading any information.

| 2
a| Fill the environment structure, pack it, and update the environment record:

* EnvVersionNumber = 1
* EnvApplicationNumber = number generated by the server, initialized with its start time (in seconds) and incremented at each personalization
* EnvIssuingDate = current date
* EnvEndDate = first day of the month of the current date + 6 years
* HolderCompany, HolderIdNumber, and EnvPadding filled with 0

| 3
| Clear the event record (update with a byte array filled with 0).

| 4
| Clear all the contract records (update with byte arrays filled with 0).

| 5
| Clear the counter file (update with a byte array filled with 0).

| 6
| Close the session.

| 7
| Return the status of the operation to the upper layer. `<Exit process>`
|===

==== Storage cards

The environment block(s) are written, and the event and contract blocks are filled with 0, without secure session (steps 1 and 6 not applicable). The counter being stored in the contract record, the step 5 is not applicable.

[[loading-procedure]]
=== Contract loading

Executed by the sales server, with its SAM (see <<loading-use-case>>). The procedure has two parts: the analysis of the contracts, whose result is displayed to the user, then the writing of the contract chosen by the user.

==== Contract analysis

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

| 1
| Open a secure session at the Load access level, reading the environment record. The demo also reads the event, the contracts, and the counters in this session, then closes it.

| 2
| Unpack the environment structure.

| 3
| If EnvVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card (card not personalized). `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 4
| If EnvEndDate is in the past, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 5
| Read and unpack the last event record.

| 6
| If EventVersionNumber is not the expected one (0 for a blank card, 1 for the current version), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 7
| Store the ContractPriority fields of the event in a persistent object, with a flag indicating a change of priority, set to false.

| 8
| For each contract record:

| 8.1
| Read and unpack the contract record.

| 8.2
| If ContractVersionNumber is 0 (blank record), set the associated ContractPriority to 0 and move on to the next contract.

| 8.3
| If ContractAuthenticator is not 0, verify its value with the PSO Verify Signature command of the SAM. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 8.3.1
| If the value is wrong, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 8.3.2
| If ContractSaleSam is on the black list of the SAMs, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 8.4
| If ContractValidityEndDate is in the past, set the associated ContractPriority to 31 and set the change flag to true.

| 8.5
| Add the contract to the list of the contracts of the card.

| 9
| Return the list of the contracts. `<Exit process>`
|===

The user then chooses the contract to load (type, and number of trips of a multi-trip ticket), and presents the card again. The server reads it again (step 1) and recomputes the ContractPriority fields (steps 7, 8.2, and 8.4), without repeating the checks of the steps 3 to 6.

==== Writing of the contract and update of the priorities

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

| 10
a| Fill the contract structure to write:

* ContractVersionNumber = 1
* ContractTariff = value provided by the upper layer (1 or 2; any other value is rejected)
* ContractSaleDate = current date

| 10.1
| If the operation is the renewal of a season pass (ContractTariff = 1), ContractValidityEndDate = original ContractValidityEndDate + 30 days if the season pass has not expired, or ContractSaleDate + 30 days if it has expired.

| 10.2
| Otherwise, ContractValidityEndDate = ContractSaleDate + 30 days for a season pass (ContractTariff = 1), or EnvEndDate for a multi-trip ticket (ContractTariff = 2).

| 11
| Pack the contract structure.

| 12
| If the traceability mode is enabled, generate the authenticator with the PSO Generate Signature command of the SAM. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 13
| If a contract of the same type (ContractTariff) is present on the card, even expired, the operation is a renewal: use the index of this contract.

| 14.1
| If its ContractPriority is equal to ContractTariff, go to `CNT_UPD`.

| 14.2
| Otherwise, set its ContractPriority to ContractTariff and set the change flag to true.

| 15
| Otherwise (new contract):

| 15.1
| If one or more ContractPriority fields are 0, the record with the lowest index receives the contract. Set its ContractPriority to ContractTariff, set the change flag to true, and go to `CNT_UPD`.

| 15.2
| Otherwise, if a ContractPriority field is 31, the first one gives the record that receives the contract. Set its ContractPriority to ContractTariff, set the change flag to true, and go to `CNT_UPD`.

| 15.3
| Otherwise (no empty nor expired record), reject the card (card full). `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 15.4
| On the single-contract cards (Calypso Basic, storage cards), the steps 15.1 to 15.3 are replaced by: the contract is replaced only if it is empty, expired, or exhausted (multi-trip ticket without trips left); otherwise, reject the card (card full). `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 16
| `CNT_UPD`: open a secure session at the Load access level, and update the contract record of the chosen index.

| 17
| If ContractTariff is 2, set the counter of the contract to its current value (0 for a new contract) increased by the number of trips provided by the upper layer. This number must be positive, and the counter cannot exceed 16,777,215 (24 bits); otherwise, the operation is rejected. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 18
a| If the change flag is true, fill the event structure to update:

* EventVersionNumber = 1
* EventDateStamp, EventTimeStamp, EventLocation, EventContractUsed = values of the previous event
* ContractPriority1 to ContractPriority4 = values of the persistent object
* EventPadding = 0

The demo always updates the event, its version number being set to 1 on a blank card.

| 19
| Pack the event structure and update the event record.

| 20
| Close the session.

| 21
| Return the status of the operation to the upper layer. `<Exit process>`
|===

==== Storage cards

The procedure is executed without secure session (steps 1, 16, and 20 without session). The card holding a single contract, the step 15.4 applies. The counter being stored in the contract record, it is written with the contract at the step 16 (step 17 without separate counter).

[[validation-procedure]]
=== Validation

Executed by the validation terminal, with its SAM (see <<validation-use-case>>). The ContractPriority fields of the event give the order in which the contracts are read: the best candidate is found with the fewest records read, and thus the fewest commands exchanged with the card, and a card without usable contract is detected without reading its contracts. An expired or exhausted contract gets the priority 31, so that the next validations no longer read it, until it is renewed or replaced.

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

2+| *Event analysis*

| 1
| Open a secure session at the Debit access level, reading the environment record.

| 2
| Unpack the environment structure.

| 3
| If EnvVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 4
| If EnvEndDate is in the past, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 5
| Read and unpack the last event record.

| 6
| If EventVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card (0: card never loaded). `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 6.1
| Anti-passback (see <<anti-passback-rule>>): if the last event is within the anti-passback delay (1 minute), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>` The time of the event being recorded to the minute, the times are compared to the minute: the card is rejected until the end of the minute following the delay. +
Exception on the Calypso cards: if the previous validation session was interrupted by the removal of the card (session not ratified), the card is considered as validated, without new decrement: go to `END`, which closes the session.

| 7
| Store the ContractPriority fields of the event in a persistent object.

2+| *Best contract search*

| 8
| Create a list of the ContractPriority fields different from 0 and 31 (the unknown codes being excluded too).

| 9
| If the list is empty, go to `END`.

| 10
| Order the list by ContractPriority value.

| 11
| For each element of the list (the type of the contract is read in its ContractTariff field, the priorities only giving the order of the analysis):

| 11.1
| Read and unpack the contract record.

| 11.2
| If ContractVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>`

| 11.3
| If ContractAuthenticator is not 0, verify its value with the PSO Verify Signature command of the SAM. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 11.3.1
| If the value is wrong, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 11.3.2
| If ContractSaleSam is on the black list of the SAMs, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 11.4
| If ContractValidityEndDate is in the past, set the associated ContractPriority to 31, and move on to the next element of the list.

| 11.5
| If ContractTariff is 2 (multi-trip ticket):

| 11.5.1
| Read the counter associated with the contract (the counter #1 for the contract #1, and so on).

| 11.5.2
| If the counter value is 0, set the associated ContractPriority to 31, and move on to the next element of the list.

| 11.5.3
| If ContractTariff is 3 and the counter value is lower than the amount of the validation, move on to the next element of the list. _Not implemented by the demo (stored value)._

2+| *Update counter*

| 11.5.4
| Decrement the counter by 1. The contract is used: go to the step 12. A contract whose ContractTariff is neither 1 nor 2 is not validated: move on to the next element of the list.

2+| *Add new event*

| 12
a| If a contract is used, fill the event structure to update:

* EventVersionNumber = 1
* EventDateStamp, EventTimeStamp = current date and time (to the minute)
* EventLocation = location configured in the validation terminal
* EventContractUsed = index of the contract used
* ContractPriority1 to ContractPriority4 = values of the persistent object
* EventPadding = 0

| 12.1
| If no contract can be used, but ContractPriority values have been set to 31 (contracts expired or without trips left), the card is rejected: fill the event structure with the values of the previous event, except the ContractPriority fields, set to the values of the persistent object (see <<rejected-card>>).

| 13
| Pack the event structure and update the event record.

| 14
| `END`: close the session if the event has been updated (steps 12 and 12.1) or after a non-ratified session (step 6.1); otherwise, cancel it.

| 15
| Return the status of the operation to the upper layer. `<Exit process>`
|===

==== Storage cards

* *Step 1*: the environment, event, and contract blocks are read at once, without secure session.
* *Step 6.1*: no exception, the storage cards having no session to ratify.
* *Steps 7 to 11*: the card holding a single contract, there is no list of priorities: the contract is read (11.1) and checked (11.2). An expired contract (11.4), a multi-trip ticket without trips left (11.5.2), or a contract of an unknown type rejects the card, without writing.
* *Step 11.5.4*: the counter, stored in the contract record, is decremented in this record.
* *Step 12*: ContractPriority1 is set to the ContractTariff of the contract, the other priorities to 0. The step 12.1 is not applicable.
* *Steps 13 and 14*: the contract and event blocks are written, without session to close.

[[inspection-procedure]]
=== Inspection

Executed by the inspection terminal, with or without SAM (see <<inspection-use-case>>).

[cols="^1,12", options="header"]
|===
| Step | Action

2+| *Event analysis*

| 1.1
| If the SAM is available, open a secure session at the Debit access level, reading the environment record, set the inTransactionFlag to true, and go to the step 2.

| 1.2
| Otherwise, if the card supports the PKI mode, open a PKI secure session, reading the environment record, set the inTransactionFlag to true, and go to the step 2.

| 1.3
| Otherwise, read the environment record, without authentication of the card.

| 2
| Unpack the environment structure.

| 3
| If EnvVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>`

| 4
| If EnvEndDate is in the past, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>`

| 5
| Read and unpack the last event record.

| 6
| If EventVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card; if it is 0, return the status of a card never loaded ("`No ticket`"). `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>`

| 7
| If EventLocation is not the location configured in the inspection terminal, set the "`not valid`" flag of the validated contract to true, and go to `CNT_READ`.

| 8
| Otherwise, if EventDateStamp is before the current date, set the "`not valid`" flag to true, and go to `CNT_READ`.

| 9
| Otherwise, if EventTimeStamp + validation period configured in the inspection terminal is before the current time, set the "`not valid`" flag to true. The time of the event being recorded to the minute, the times are compared to the minute: the validation is valid until the end of the minute of the end of the validation period.

2+| *Contract analysis*

| 10
| `CNT_READ`: read all the contract records and the counter file.

| 11
| For each contract:

| 12
| Unpack the contract.

| 13
| If ContractVersionNumber is 0, the contract is blank: move on to the next contract.

| 14
| If ContractVersionNumber is not the expected one (1 for the current version), reject the card. `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>`

| 15
| If the SAM is available and ContractAuthenticator is not 0, verify its value with the PSO Verify Signature command of the SAM. _Not implemented by the demo._

| 15.1
| If the value is wrong, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 15.2
| If ContractSaleSam is on the black list of the SAMs, reject the card. `<Abort Transaction if inTransactionFlag is true and exit process>` _Not implemented by the demo._

| 16
| If ContractValidityEndDate is in the past, mark the contract as expired.

| 17
| If EventContractUsed is the index of the contract and the "`not valid`" flag is false, mark the contract as validated.

| 18
| If ContractTariff is 2, extract the counter value associated with the contract.

| 19
| Add the contract to the list of the contracts to return to the upper layer.

| 20
| If the inTransactionFlag is true, close the session.

| 21
| Return the status of the operation to the upper layer. `<Exit process>`
|===

==== Storage cards

* *Step 1*: the environment, event, and contract blocks are read at once, without authentication of the card (steps 1.1 and 1.2 not applicable); the MIFARE Classic 1K cards require the authentication of their sector with the key A, which gives access to the blocks but does not authenticate the card.
* *Steps 10 to 12*: the single contract, read at the step 1, is unpacked.
* *Step 18*: the counter value is read in the contract record.
* *Step 20*: the transaction ends, without session to close.
